title: Raster
description: A song title set in letters drawn only from horizontal and vertical strokes with 45-degree corners on a 5 x 9 design grid, shaded as a lit relief and rendered only by a halftone screen. Each stroke rises from its outline to a rounded crest under a point light that follows the pointer, so a stem runs from a pale lit flank to a dark shadowed one. A square raster turned to its own angle measures how much of each cell the letters cover at 8 x 8 samples in the screen's own frame, multiplies that by the shading, and prints a Euclidean spot of that size: a round dot that grows to a corner-to-corner checkerboard at half and closes to round white holes toward solid. Hover to move the light. Drag up or down for the pitch, five to twenty-eight cells across a letter; drag sideways to turn the screen from 0 to 45 degrees. At 45 the cuts lock to the screen; between, the screen crosses the shading inside every stem at an angle and moire bands slide along them. Type to change the title.
intent: After Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet (1967), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Alphabet, and his Vormgevers poster grid: accept the raster completely and let the letterforms come from it. Own glyphs, not the font.
